claims.text: Applying density functional theory with the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof exchange-correlation functional can modify the potential energy landscape of zirconia ceramic.
Modification of the zirconia potential energy landscape by this method can reduce its sintering temperature.
Modifying the material's potential energy landscape reduces the energy barrier for atomic diffusion.
Reducing the energy barrier for atomic diffusion leads to a lower sintering temperature.
The proposed intervention will reduce the sintering temperature by at least 150°C relative to conventional sintering.
The resulting sintering temperature will be below 900°C.
The magnitude of the sintering-temperature reduction may depend on material composition and sintering protocol.
A reduction of less than 50°C would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires a reduction of at least 150°C, but the hypothesis is declared falsified only below 50°C. Thus, a measured reduction from 50°C to less than 150°C would contradict the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
